definition: A model architecture that encodes two inputs (such as a query and a document) independently into separate embeddings, which can then be compared efficiently.
details: Bi-encoders enable fast large-scale retrieval because document embeddings can be precomputed and indexed, unlike cross-encoders which require joint processing of each pair at query time.
story: Imagine a factory floor where each workstation can glance at every other workstation before doing its part. It is the blueprint that makes everything else possible. At the bottom of every machine is a design — the shape of it, and how its pieces talk to each other. Structure decides what the model can even express — the blueprint before the bricks. And that shape of the machine — Bi-Encoder — is what makes everything else possible.
